The prompt the model was given

Imported verbatim from v6/mapcompletion_prompt.py. Image 1 is the plain 2025 capture; image 2 is the same capture with the existing pedestrian network drawn over it in cyan — both shown on every card below, as sent.

System

You are a geospatial analyst auditing the completeness of a pedestrian infrastructure map against aerial imagery. Respond ONLY with a single JSON object matching the provided schema. Do not add prose outside the JSON.

User

Image 1 and image 2 are the same aerial photograph of the same place at the same time. Image 2 has an existing pedestrian infrastructure map drawn over it as coloured lines and dots; image 1 is the unmarked photograph. List and concisely describe the pedestrian mobility infrastructure that is visible in the photograph but is NOT represented by the lines drawn in image 2. Judge only what you can see: do not report infrastructure that is already drawn, and do not report features that are not pedestrian mobility infrastructure. Provide locations with coordinates of range (0,0) at the bottom-left to (1,1) at the top-right, read against the photograph. If the drawn map is already complete, output an empty `missing` list.

Map completion — Anacortes, 20 tiles

The model saw an unmarked aerial photograph and the same photograph with the existing pedestrian network drawn over it, and was asked what pedestrian infrastructure is visible but not drawn. Its answers are in blue. The reviewed CNN proposals are coloured by the reviewer’s verdict: orange where they were accepted as real and unmapped, pink where they were rejected, pink dashed where the reviewer was unsure. The orange ones are the answer key.
